analysis.title: Vodafone (VOD.L): 2Q27 revenue growth beat, with modest FY27 guidance raise reflecting underlying growth and faster efficiency efforts
key_insights: Vodafone 2Q27 group organic service revenue growth (OSRG) was 6.4% vs Visible Alpha consensus 4.7%, a 1.7pp beat. GS expects a positive share price reaction.
Group revenues were EUR 11,559mn vs consensus EUR 11,424mn (+1.2%). Group service revenues were EUR 9,783mn vs EUR 9,611mn (+1.8%).
The OSRG beat came from the UK and Turkey/Africa, with Germany in line. GS sees most of the beat as driven by sustainable growth drivers.
UK OSRG was 1.2% vs 0.4% consensus. The acceleration vs 1Q27 (0.6%) came from improved B2B performance, likely sustainable, and higher roaming revenues, which are less sustainable.
Africa and Turkey beats continue and look increasingly structural. Vodacom OSRG was 14.0% vs 11.1% consensus. Turkey service revenue growth was 35.2% vs 30.2% in 1Q27.
Other Europe OSRG was 1.8% vs 0.6% consensus, largely from B2B. The key driver, Greece, appears to reflect contract phasing, which is less sustainable.
Germany OSRG was -0.5% vs -0.6% consensus, down from +1.2% in 1Q27. Broadband net adds were -100k and postpaid net adds were +10k.
Germany EBITDA includes a EUR 100mn FY27 hit from the ECJ ruling. GS believes consensus already includes about EUR 50mn of it. Europe guidance was not changed despite the hit.

Group FY27 guidance was raised: adj. EBITDAaL to EUR 13.2-13.4bn (from the upper end of EUR 13.0-13.3bn) and adj. FCF to EUR 2.8-3.0bn (from the upper end of EUR 2.6-2.9bn). This implies about a 2% uplift to consensus FCF.
UK VOD/3 synergies are now guided to GBP 150mn, up from GBP 100mn.

Net cost efficiencies are guided to EUR 200mn for FY27, against EUR 1bn net over four years from the EUR 2bn gross programme. GS reads this as positive because the net savings were expected to be back-end loaded.
Vodafone booked significant non-cash impairments, particularly in Germany, driven primarily by higher interest rates.
GS sees material upside to consensus and Group returns from improved UK growth as the mobile market repairs into CY28, and from cost efficiency upside. Rated Buy.
1H27 EBITDAaL missed consensus: Group EUR 6,451mn vs EUR 6,508mn (-0.9%), Europe -2.6%, Other Europe -8.2%. Adj. FCF was EUR -440mn vs EUR 2mn consensus.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after a 2Q27 revenue beat and an FY27 guidance raise, citing UK repair, cost efficiency upside and strong Turkey/Africa growth. The ADR was $15.69 at the 9 Nov close, 33.4% upside.

sector_views.rationale: The report gives no sector-level stance. It covers Vodafone only, with UK mobile market repair expected into CY28.

earnings_insights: Vodafone 2Q27 (reported 10 Nov 2026): group OSRG 6.4% actual vs 4.7% Visible Alpha consensus. Group revenues EUR 11,559mn actual vs EUR 11,424mn consensus.
1H27 Group EBITDAaL EUR 6,451mn actual vs EUR 6,508mn Visible Alpha consensus (-0.9%). 1H27 adj. FCF EUR -440mn actual vs EUR 2mn consensus.

FY27 guidance, company-compiled consensus in brackets: Europe EBITDAaL EUR 7.6-7.9bn (7,817mn), Group adj. EBITDAaL EUR 13.2-13.4bn (13,284mn), Group adj. FCF EUR 2.8-3.0bn (2,836mn). Guidance is 0.1%, 0.9% and 5.8% above consensus respectively.
GS estimates: FY3/27E EPS EUR 0.18, revenue EUR 44,789mn, EBIT EUR 7,822mn. FY3/28E EPS EUR 0.13. P/E is 7.7x for FY3/27E.
FY27 guidance includes Safaricom and assumes EUR 1 = GBP 0.86, ZAR 18.82, TRY 54.8, EGP 58.99.
risk_factors: Higher-than-expected competition in the German market
